summary: Backend-only check of the BITSAT chapter-wise fix in tejas/book_reader.py (READER_VERSION 7). I reproduced it on read-only copies of the customer's books with the in-memory harness, which writes nothing to the DB. Logical Reasoning (1119 pages): 18 mocks x 50 questions, all mcq. Only 36 issues remain: 18 'Confirm printed examination rules' and 18 'Choose the subject', both caused by the harness lacking production destination defaults. Before the fix the harness gave 3568 issues. Chemistry (2167 pages): 32 mocks x 50 questions, all mcq, 32 issues, all 'Confirm printed examination rules' (before: 4936). In both books there are 0 page issues and no key, solution or option issues. I compared every answer with the printed Q01..Q50 answer-key page (found through the PDF bookmarks and parsed separately with fitz): 900/900 LR and 1600/1600 chemistry match. LR Chapter 1 reads Q01-05 as A,B,C,A,C. Every question has a solution region, and Mock 1 solution_kind is supplied_worked. Chemistry Chapters 8 ('Solutions') and 32 have full-height crops (0.747), with no crop under 0.15 anywhere. The 'crop contains another question number' flags (17 LR, 2 chem) are false alarms from the harness: they are numbered statements ('1. Some captains...') or a wrapped '16)'. Each question has a page to itself, so the 'taller than 60%' flag is expected. Regressions: the AITS 2-mock book has 2 ready mocks and 0 issues, with pages question 75 / key 1 / solution 75. The JEE chapter-wise chemistry replay is IDENTICAL to cold_chemistry_chapterwise.log (empty diff). Existing suites: regressions178 29/29, key_table_split190 12/12, reread_iso179 15/15. The code review found two real edge-case problems, both confirmed with synthetic test pages: (1) in a book whose solutions are plain 'N.'-numbered, one stray matching solution line drops the rest of the book's solutions; (2) ruled key tables with fewer than 10 rows per column are not read.

minor.issue: Regression in v7, confirmed on synthetic pages (works under v6). Take a book whose solutions are plain 'N.'-numbered. If one solution begins with something like '2. Solution: a mixture...', '5. Ans 4' or '7. Answer: because...', ANSWERED matches it. ANSWERED uses re.I, so [A-D] also matches the lowercase words a/b/c/d. That one match sets solution_style='answer', which then stays on for the rest of the book because plan_start does not clear it. From then on every other solution anchor is dropped. The text from those dropped solutions joins the previous solution, so it is mis-attached silently (test result: page 1 solutions [1,2,3] became [2]; page 2 [4,5] became [2]). Possible fix: make [A-D] case-sensitive or require the brackets '(A)'. Only switch to answer style when most of the page's anchors (or at least 2) match. Consider clearing solution_style at each mock/plan_start.

On a bookmark key page with a 2-column 'Q01 ... A' table, a column is only read if it has at least 10 rows. A chapter with 19 or fewer questions in 2 columns (or a 3-column layout) gets 0 pairs. The fallback key_cells(body,1) is skipped because 'Q01' counts as a question anchor, so those keys go unread. The BITSAT books have 50 questions per chapter, so they are not affected.

Only in plan mode: a line equal to the chapter title is always ignored. Suppose a chapter is titled 'Solutions' or 'Answer Key' and its bookmarks mark only where the chapter starts, with no Questions/Answer key/Solutions parts. Then the real role heading of that name would be skipped too. In the BITSAT books the bookmarks name each part, so this does not happen there. Low risk.

action_items: Harden the ANSWERED / solution_style='answer' switch so one stray 'N. Solution: a...' or 'N. Ans 4' line cannot remove the solutions of a plain-numbered book. Ideas: case-sensitive (A)-(D), a majority or at-least-2 rule, reset at each mock. Re-run python tests/reader_v7_edges213.py; it should print RESULT OK.
Optional: lower the ruled='only' rule of at least 10 rows per column (for example to 5 when the page is a bookmark key page) so short chapters' keys are read.
critical_code_review_comments: ANSWERED uses re.I, so [A-D] also matches lowercase a-d words. The match is too loose to switch the parsing mode for the whole book.
solution_style is never cleared between mocks or chapters ('q' already behaved this way; 'answer' now does too).
The ruled='only' path is used only in the bookmark-plan key branch (line 329). The other key_cells callers are unchanged, and the identical replay confirms the non-plan path is not affected.
The 'q' branch runs before the ANSWERED branch, so books headed 'Question N' are safe, as claimed.
book_reader.py is 518 lines, still under 700. The code is dense one-liners.

Run long jobs with nohup in the background and poll; a foreground '&' with setsid can hang the tool. LR takes about 2 min and chem about 3 min. Then run python tests/bitsat_key_audit213.py <pdf> <audit.json> 'Chapter 8' to check answers against the printed keys. Expect 0 mismatches.
rca of the issue: Confirmed what E1 reported. The BITSAT key pages print a ruled 'Q01 ... A' table; 'Q01' was taken for a question anchor, so no keys were read. Worked solutions '1. Answer (A)' contain numbered steps, which were split off as separate solutions. Chapter titles printed on question pages ('Solutions', 'Chemistry in Everyday Life') were read as role/subject headings, so each crop shrank to a sliver. With v7 the issue counts drop from 3568 to 36 (LR) and from 4936 to 32 (chem). The remaining issues come from missing destination defaults in the harness.
